title: Daisy motif — layered petals
subtitle: Two rings of petals in contrasting lengths give depth and a fuller flower, 11 cm
excerpt: A second inner ring of shorter petals sits between and behind the eight outer petals, giving the flower depth without any three-dimensional techniques. The inner petals peek out between the outer ones, producing a layered effect visible from the front. At 11 cm it works as an applique flower on cushion covers, bags, and garment panels.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), layered flower motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), flower crochet section.
heroPrompt: A layered daisy crochet motif with two rings of petals — cream outer petals and pale blush inner petals — on a natural linen background in soft daylight. 11 cm, layered effect visible, photographed flat from above.

chartDefinition.title: Daisy motif — layered petals
chartDefinition.caption: Centre ring, inner petal ring (6-chain foundations, shorter), then outer petal ring (10-chain foundations, longer). Inner petals are worked first so they sit behind the outer ring.

glossaryTerms.definition: A loop formed by joining a length of chain with a slip stitch — the centre foundation for flat flower motifs.

content.text: The layered daisy works an inner ring of eight shorter petals before the outer ring, so they sit behind and between the outer petals. The inner petals use a 6-chain foundation and two dc rows; the outer petals use a 10-chain foundation and three dc rows. The centre
chain ring
has 16 dc to give both petal rings enough anchor points without crowding.

Work the inner petals first, in the contrast colour, so they are covered from the front by the outer petals when both are flat. If you work the outer ring first and try to add the inner ring behind, the inner petals tend to push forward.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 4 g of inner-petal colour plus 6 g of outer-petal colour — all DK-weight cotton. A small amount of a third colour for the centre. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished layered daisy measures 11 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-press.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
Pattern
Centre ring
In centre colour: Ch 6. Sl st to first ch to form a ring. Ch 1. Work 16dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. (16 dc.) Drop centre colour.
Inner petals — 8 petals in contrast colour

Join inner-petal colour to any dc of the ring. *Ch 6. Turn. Sk first ch, dc across next 4 ch. (4 dc.) Turn. Ch 1. Dc across all 4 sts. (4 dc.) Sl st into next dc of centre ring.* Repeat from * to * seven more times to complete 8 inner petals. Fasten off inner-petal colour.
Outer petals — 8 petals in main colour

Join main petal colour to the same dc where the inner-petal round began, working between two inner petals. *Ch 10. Turn. Sk first ch, dc across next 8 ch. (8 dc.) Turn. Ch 1. Dc across all 8 sts. (8 dc.) Turn. Ch 1. Dc across all 8 sts. (8 dc.) Sl st into next dc of centre ring (skipping one dc to allow the inner petal to sit behind).* Repeat from * to * seven more times. After 8th outer petal, sl st to starting dc. Fasten off.

definition.title: Daisy motif — layered petals
definition.caption: Centre ring of 16dc. Inner petals: ch-6 foundations, 2 rows of 4dc. Outer petals: ch-10 foundations, 3 rows of 8dc.

content.text: Finishing

Weave in all ends through the back of the nearest petals. A light steam-press flattens any petal curl. Separate the inner and outer petals gently with your fingers before pressing to ensure both rings are visible from the front.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat on a towel and ease petal layers into position while damp.
What to try next

The bobble-centre daisy (crochet-daisy-bobble-centre) raises the centre into three dimensions with a cluster of bobble stitches. The rose motifs (crochet-rose-rolled, crochet-rose-layered) extend the layered-petal idea into a spiral rather than a flat ring.
